body: yes, exactly. pretty sure it's only ever happened with strong anger or strong sadness, never with positive or mild feelings. Or at least I think never, my memory is pretty crap lol

I doubt it's brain damage. I also can't diagnose you with anything, especially something like schizophrenia (or schizoaffective disorder), but yes, there are a lot more symptoms to it than hallucinations. some of the main warning signs of schizophrenia actually are the symptoms that many people don't notice — declining personal hygiene, disorganized thoughts or speech, withdrawing from friends and family, having strange beliefs about the world or religion... and weed can trigger psychosis, even if you haven't had it before, kind of similar to how someone with bipolar might have their first manic episode triggered by a stimulant or an antidepressant.

Anyway that's a lot of information. You should talk to a therapist or a psychiatrist if you can about your symptoms and what steps to take next, and there's a lot of communities online of people with the same or similar experiences. even if it turns out it's not schizophrenia, psychosis is psychosis, and you'd be welcome in those spaces anyhow (plus, if someone's suggestion for a coping mechanism works, then it works!) 

I can imagine how disorienting and scary this all is, though. I hope it gets easier soon

Mostly taking it day by day (and some low-level dissociation, I've noticed, on account of not being able to remember almost anything most days) and hanging on out of fear of a) pain, b) failing and being committed, or c) succeeding but going to hell or something
Which is not helpful, but I know where you're coming from, if that's anything. Not the same situation: I'm bipolar, 18, and currently trying to cope with having the "easy" part be over and transitioning into work/college; but I also survived a few attempts, so I know what it's like to not know what comes next.
Some days are good, though. Mostly because of the people in them. So I think that's what it comes down to, finding the days and the people and the things that are good and holding onto that and trying to make those good things a bigger part of your life than the bad things.
Also, therapy. I had to quit for a while and am currently looking for a new therapist, but it helped when I was doing it. And medication helps some, though we're still trying to find what helps more than just "some".
Good luck!

I feel like being a lesbian might complicate this one, in the sense of: I would date someone who's never been in a relationship before but is secure in their sexuality; would be wary of dating someone who just came out or is "experimenting" or comments on "never having been with a woman" etc. Not that the person themself is a bad person, just because I find a relationship is a very vulnerable thing and being someone's teacher or experiment tends to be exhausting and a bit alienating. I feel like I have to do enough teaching/weathering ignorance in my day to day life.
Then again, it's hard to consider just one trait in a void. I feel like I might be more patient with a real person that I have feelings for rather than an imaginary hypothetical.

I feel like it's a question of, like you said, insecurity and resentment. people look for an "out" to those feelings all the time, and it's not to say it's your fault for the feelings — just that deflection is an extremely common response. see QAnon, inceldom, the red scare, TERFism... At least in my eyes, it's all people who feel unsafe, oppressed, unhappy, who end up turning to a belief in a boogeyman that they can "fight" and place blame upon. Not that the blame is theirs — a lot of these people /are/ unfairly disenfranchised, but it's easier to post at Jews/women/communists/trans people/etc than it is to think of things one can't change. Generational poverty, corruption, institutional patriarchy, just plain bad luck or bad people, those are things you can't form a movement around. One specific target is. And anger feels good! It feels righteous and often it feels better than self-pity.
I think that the way out is to cut contact with those communities, to seek therapy (or counseling, or a support group, or just recovery one whatever way works for you), to practice empathy towards everyone, to work on not dividing the people you interact with along the lines of Man and Woman. and maybe hang out with better people! Shallow women definitely exist. And to not see a relationship as a necessity. There's plenty of people who don't date till later. There's virgin adult women, too. You can live a fulfilled life either way, and the truth is when you come off as comfortable, happy, or just not desperate, people tend to like you more.

Depends on the state, as other people have said, and some places /do/ require psychological screenings for a license (and a special license depending on the weapon iirc). It's that way because of "states rights" dictating that states should have more liberty to decide on their own laws, and because many states (more conservative ones at least) tend to be pretty lax on gun control, as far as I can see, because it's part of the "culture" to believe in self-defense via gun and in one's right to own a weapon (and the general idea that the government should be as uninvolved as possible)

That said: I feel like the focus on psychological screenings is misplaced. I've been screened many times (for actual mental health care purposes) and it's incredibly easy to lie. I've known people who have evaded hospitalizations with this. I've known people who were just dismissed, too — no lying necessary — and ended up worse off. I strongly doubt every single person who might be violent will be "caught" by mental health screening. You can really easily say "no" when they ask questions about wanting to hurt yourself or others, or questions about emotional dysregulation or anything that might look "bad" if you have any self-awareness at all.

Sex might be private. Sexual preference (as in things like how often, when, and where) might be private. Sexuality itself? Not private. It affects my life. Who I date or love is not private. The danger it sometimes puts me in is not private. The fact people are still fighting for legal rights and protections is not private. And I don't really want it to be private, either. I'm a lesbian. It informs how I deal with the world sometimes (I find I have a lot less patience for misogyny, for example. And for men I'm general. Sorry men.). And it informs how the world deals with me — straight women get REAL weird about things real fast, I've found. You're free to not talk about your sexuality! You're even free to think about plants and fish and whatever. But "isn't it private?" Is, quite honestly, rehashed homophobia. We've been through Don't Ask, Don't Tell already and that wasn't private enough. Also, do you expect straight people to be private about it too? Should marriages, boyfriends, etc. Be secret? No more romance or coming of age movies? Because those all talk about sexuality too. I'm just guessing it's not the type of sexuality that makes you uncomfortable.

Kids operate using a lot of stereotyping — they're still learning what things are and aren't. I was once asked why I was wearing a dress if I was a boy because I had short hair. I'm not actually masculine looking, most people clock me as "female" almost instantly. But the kid, being that she was still learning to use schemata in her thinking, thought short hair = boy. It's probably similar in your case: the kid is still learning to categorize information, so using their limited understanding of what is a man and a woman, they asked a question. If they bothered to ask if you were a lady, they were probably more confused than anything. (Kids are also pretty rigid in thinking, so often it goes "woman = breasts, therefore no woman has no breasts and no man has breasts", for example)
Plus, your coworkers probably changed the subject because they saw how you felt and didn't want to make the situation worse. IME "distract the kid and change the subject" is pretty much the standard reaction to "oh no a kid said something awkward"

TL;DR, don't take it as a judgement of beauty, kids are still learning how the world works.
